tier_rationale: Malody Key mode is a continuous falling-note rhythm game: notes, chords, jacks, and hold heads/tails arrive on a clock while the player is deciding. The documented standard-C Big-P window is only about 40 ms and the G/miss boundary is about 200 ms, so an Astra call taking seconds cannot be in the per-note control loop and even a roughly 0.5-second Jev call is too slow for dense charts. The adaptor must schedule known chart events in code and use Astra for planning/adaptation and Jev for bounded fast recognition.

interface.why: A local deterministic Key-mode emulator is the only practical route under the supplied offline headless Linux, no-display, no-GPU, no-audio, and no-account constraints. It can parse native .mc charts, expose structured JSON, accept timestamped press/release actions, and vary charts and difficulty by seed without client login or render latency. The public RM timing/score article supplies a documented proxy, while the files must label score fidelity limits because it is not a complete official Key scoring specification.
software: Python standard library: json, math, random, dataclasses, hashlib
setup_steps: Implement an in-process Python API or line-delimited JSON process in the supplied evaluator venv; do not require wall-clock sleep, audio, a display, a GPU, or network access.
Parse and validate native .mc JSON: require meta.mode == 0, read meta.mode_ext.column, validate note columns and endbeat holds, and preserve fractional beats until piecewise BPM conversion.
Build cumulative beat-to-millisecond timing segments from time[].bpm and apply the chart/audio offset exactly once; produce stable note IDs, start_ms, end_ms, columns, and tap/hold kinds.
Implement reset(seed, options) so held-out seeds deterministically vary key count, BPM, offset, density, patterns, holds, and configured judge/mod without using online charts.
Expose observations with upcoming structured notes, held columns, current logical time, judgments, signed offsets, combo, misses, broken holds, weighted accuracy, score proxy, and done status.
Accept press(column, at_ms), release(column, at_ms), advance(to_ms), and timestamp-sorted event batches; resolve chords at one timestamp and auto-miss overdue notes after the configured deadline.
Use the documented C/A-E timing table and accuracy weights; label the 200/332/466/600 combo score and multipliers as rm_proxy_2025 rather than official Key scoring.
Optionally use the Malody V replay renderer only for post-hoc validation if an authorized .mrv and chart package are supplied; it is not required for the evaluator.
interface.observation: Structured JSON, not pixels: episode seed/mode/key count/judge/mod/logical time, chart BPM segments and offset, at least the next 1-2 seconds or 64 notes grouped by start time with column/start/end/kind, held columns, last judgments with signed offsets, and score/accuracy/combo/miss/broken-hold statistics.
interface.actions: Timestamped JSON actions: press(column, at_ms) for tap/hold heads, release(column, at_ms) for hold tails, advance(to_ms) to progress and resolve misses, or a sorted batch of these events. Chords require simultaneous presses in their columns; the adaptor schedules exact chart timestamps rather than waiting in real time.

scoring: Report weighted judgment accuracy as the primary score: Big P=1.00, p1=0.90, p2=0.85, p3=0.80, G=0.40, M=0.00, plus judgment histogram, misses, broken holds, max combo, and completion. Also report the documented D/no-mod RM-compatible score proxy using 200/332/466/600 Big-P combo bases and judge/mod multipliers, explicitly labelled rm_proxy_2025; the source is https://m.mugzone.net/wiki/2443?lang=sc and applies to RM mode, so it must not be presented as verified native Key scoring.
scenarios: reset(seed) must generate or select deterministic native-mode-0 charts while holding out whole pattern families. Vary 4K-7K key counts, constant and changing BPM, positive/negative offsets, snap resolution, isolated taps, alternation/streams, same-lane jacks, chords, anchors, holds and final releases, density/difficulty, and no-mod/Flip/Const options. Use perfect scripted actions for parser/scorer checks and controlled early/late/noisy actions for timing-window checks. Do not depend on network chart downloads or user accounts; the native chart schema is described at https://prefixaut.github.io/rconv/rconv/malody.html and https://github.com/Jakads/malody2osu/blob/master/convert.py.
strategy_summary: Preprocess the complete chart in code, convert fractional beats through every BPM segment, and schedule timestamped lane presses/releases; do not ask Astra or Jev to react to individual notes. Group equal-time notes into chords, alternate/pace streams and jacks, and keep holds down through endbeat, with C judge/no mod as the calibration baseline. Astra should select difficulty/judge/mod and diagnose signed timing, chord, jack, or hold-specific errors from structured summaries; Jev should only answer fast typed pattern/risk choices over a JSON horizon. Evaluate accuracy and combo across seeded charts, while treating the documented RM score formula as a labelled proxy rather than verified Key scoring.
risks: The official Steam client is a Windows GUI build with a Mugzone account requirement; no supported Linux headless gameplay API was found.

Public timing and score documentation is for RM mode, while the requested target is Key mode; the emulator must expose this fidelity limitation and calibrate against an authorized real client if exact Key scores matter.
Real-client screen/input automation has GUI timing jitter, audio/GPU/display dependencies, account and possible anti-cheat/ToS exposure, and is not selected.
Native .mc format references are community parsers rather than one complete official specification; unusual time signatures, negative snaps, effects, and modern chart versions require validation.
Replay rendering is post-hoc and does not control a live game; chart APIs and local servers provide files/data, not gameplay actions.
Astra/Jev model latency is longer than the strict judgment window, so a model-per-note design will fail unless the code layer schedules the known chart.
